scenes.text: At the coat hook in the thoracic gallery, imagine an extra lung parcel wearing its own coat. Keep this same hook as the permanent location for extralobar sequestration.

scenes.text: Pulmonary sequestration is abnormal lung tissue without the usual connection to the tracheobronchial tree. It receives arterial blood from the systemic circulation, commonly through an aortic branch.
scenes.spokenText: Pulmonary sequestration is abnormal lung tissue without the usual connection to the tracheobronchial tree. It receives arterial blood from the systemic circulation, commonly through an aortic branch.

scenes.text: Extralobar means the sequestered tissue has a separate visceral pleural covering. In the operative photograph, focus on the distinct pleural envelope around the lesion.

scenes.text: An intralobar sequestration instead lies within the surrounding lung and shares its pleural covering. The difference tested here is the relationship to visceral pleura.

scenes.text: Use the relationship to pleura to identify the extralobar form, and keep the feeding vessel as a separate anatomical feature. This distinction makes the question much easier.

scenes.text: Return to the coat hook and say: extra means an extra coat. In this lesson, that coat represents its own visceral pleura. Retrieve the feature before choosing an answer.
